pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Alaska Journeyman Electrician Certificate of Fitness exam is handled through the Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development Mechanical Inspection testing process. Alaska’s official testing information states that applicants must have their application packet processed and approved before scheduling a test. Department testing is offered in Anchorage, Juneau, and Fairbanks on the first and third Wednesday of each month, and proctored testing may also be available in other Alaska cities through Department of Labor Job Centers. Alaska’s official Mechanical Inspection testing information states that there is a four-hour maximum time limit on all exams. It also states that a score of at least 70 percent is required for passing all tests except Boiler Operator 2nd Class. Electrical Journeyman is listed by Alaska as an open-book National Electrical Code exam in the Mechanical Inspection study guide information. Because this exam is code-based, candidates should be comfortable using the National Electrical Code as a working reference.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The NEC is organized by articles, parts, sections, tables, definitions, exceptions, and informational notes. Candidates who only read the code passively may still struggle under timed conditions. Strong preparation should include repeated practice locating rules, using tables, reading exceptions carefully, and applying requirements to the facts presented in each question. Important preparation areas for journeyman electrician candidates commonly include general electrical knowledge, electrical theory, conductors and cables, wiring methods, raceways and boxes, grounding and bonding, overcurrent protection, motors, services, feeders, branch circuits, equipment installation, safety, load calculations, and code definitions. This Ultimate Combo gives candidates multiple study tools to review those areas from different angles. The 2026 Alaska Journeyman Electrician Study Guide helps organize broad exam topics into a more manageable study format. The 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide gives added practice for formula-based and math-heavy subjects.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The 2026 NEC Paperback with Tabs helps candidates build speed when locating code sections. Flash cards support memory and repetition, while the online test success kit helps candidates practice with exam-style questions and identify areas that need more review.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Alaska Electrical Journeyman study guide information from the Mechanical Inspection testing page identifies the exam as open book with the National Electrical Code. Open book testing gives candidates access to the code book, but it does not remove the need for preparation. In many ways, an open-book electrical exam places more emphasis on knowing how to use the code book efficiently. Candidates should study with the code book from the beginning. When working through practice questions, look up the supporting rule instead of relying only on memory. Read the full section, check nearby exceptions, review related tables, and confirm that the answer matches the exact facts in the question. This method helps build the code-navigation habits needed for timed testing. The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs is especially useful for open-book preparation. Tabs can help candidates move more quickly between commonly used code sections, but they are most effective when the candidate already understands how the NEC is arranged.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: Use the tabs during study sessions, not just on exam day, so the book becomes familiar before the official test. Open-book exams can still be challenging because the time limit requires both accuracy and pace. A candidate who spends too long searching for every answer may run out of time. A candidate who relies only on memory may miss questions that require careful code wording. The best approach combines trade knowledge, calculation practice, and efficient code lookup.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Alaska issues an Electrical Journeyman Certificate of Fitness rather than using the same licensing structure found in every other state. The Mechanical Inspection Section verifies training, experience, and registration requirements, conducts testing, and issues Certificates of Fitness in the electrical and plumbing trades. For the Electrical Journeyman Certificate of Fitness, Alaska’s application materials state that an applicant must have 8,000 hours of work in the trade. At least 6,000 hours must be commercial or industrial experience. Up to 2,000 hours may be residential experience. Alaska also allows up to 1,000 hours of trade-related classroom training to be substituted for 1,000 hours of the required commercial or industrial hours. Maintenance hours do not apply toward the Electrical Journeyman Certificate of Fitness requirement. The licensing path generally begins with gaining qualifying electrical work experience under appropriate supervision. Candidates should keep organized records of employment, work performed, hours, and training.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: When ready to apply, the candidate submits the Electrical and Plumbing Certificate of Fitness application materials, experience verification, and required payment to the Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development Mechanical Inspection Section. Alaska’s testing information states that the application packet must be processed and approved before a test can be scheduled. After approval, the candidate may schedule the exam through the Department’s testing process. A government-issued picture ID must be presented at the time of testing. After passing and completing any remaining state requirements, the applicant may proceed with the Certificate of Fitness issuance process.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Alaska’s Electrical Journeyman Certificate of Fitness authorizes the holder to perform work that is subject to the standards of the National Electrical Code as established under Alaska law and regulation. The state’s Certificate of Fitness process is administered through the Department of Labor and Workforce Development Mechanical Inspection Section. The official Alaska application materials list the Electrical Journeyman Certificate of Fitness hourly requirement as 8,000 hours of work in the trade. A minimum of 6,000 hours must be commercial or industrial. A maximum of 2,000 hours may be residential. Up to 1,000 hours of trade-related classroom training may be substituted for 1,000 hours of the commercial or industrial requirement. Maintenance hours do not apply. Applicants should use the current Alaska Electrical and Plumbing Certificate of Fitness application materials when preparing to apply. Incomplete applications may be rejected, so candidates should make sure experience verification, required forms, identification details, and payment are complete before submission.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Alaska’s Mechanical Inspection forms and testing pages are the appropriate places to review current application documents and testing instructions. Alaska also offers other electrical certificate classifications, including Residential Electrician and Electrical Trainee. Candidates preparing for the Journeyman Electrician Certificate of Fitness should make sure they are following the requirements for the journeyman classification, not a different certificate category.

pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: This Ultimate Combo supports a complete study routine by combining printed study resources with online practice. Candidates can begin with the Alaska Journeyman Electrician Study Guide to review trade topics and then use the Electrician Calculations Study Guide to focus on math-heavy areas. Electrical calculations often require careful reading and a step-by-step approach. Repeated practice helps candidates improve accuracy and avoid common mistakes caused by rushing. The National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs should be used throughout the study process. Candidates should practice locating definitions, articles, tables, wiring method rules, grounding and bonding requirements, overcurrent protection provisions, service and feeder rules, and equipment-specific requirements. The more familiar the code book becomes during study, the more useful it becomes during an open-book exam. Flash cards are helpful for short, repeated review sessions. They can be used between longer study periods to reinforce terms, concepts, formulas, and code organization.

pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials

The Online Test Success Kit helps candidates work with exam-style questions and practice applying what they have reviewed. Practice questions should be treated as learning tools. When an answer is missed, candidates should review the reason, locate the related code section when applicable, and add the topic to a follow-up study list. This process helps turn mistakes into targeted review. A strong study schedule should include a mix of reading, code lookup, calculations, flash card review, and timed practice. Candidates should not wait until the final week to begin using the NEC. Code navigation is a skill, and it improves with repetition.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Alaska electrical administrator exams are scheduled through PSI after a candidate obtains approval from the State of Alaska. The State of Alaska requires applicants to submit a complete application with supporting documentation before registering for the examination. Once approved, candidates may schedule through PSI, with Alaska test locations including Anchorage, Fairbanks, and Juneau. For the Alaska Unlimited Commercial Wiring Administrator exam, the current PSI candidate bulletin lists 100 questions , a 70% passing score , and 240 minutes of testing time. The content outline includes general electrical knowledge, grounding and bonding, services, feeders and branch circuits, raceways and enclosures, conductors and cables, special occupancies, electrical power, motors, low voltage, lighting, photovoltaics, alarm systems, safety, and Alaska statutes and regulations. This Ultimate Combo supports those exam knowledge areas by giving you multiple ways to study. The Alaska Master Electrician Study Guide provides structured review.

pieces.t: The Electrician Calculations Study Guide helps strengthen math-based problem solving. The 2026 NEC paperback with tabs supports code navigation practice. The Master Electrician Flash Cards help reinforce repeated recall. The Online Test Success Kit gives you exam-style questions and online practice to help sharpen timing, accuracy, and confidence. Exam candidates should be prepared for both code-based questions and trade knowledge questions. A strong study routine should include reading code sections, practicing with realistic questions, reviewing missed answers, using tabs consistently, and working calculations until formulas and setup methods become familiar. This package is designed to support that complete preparation process.

pieces.t: The Alaska electrical administrator examination allows specific reference materials into the examination center. Candidates are responsible for bringing their own allowed references. Reference materials may be highlighted, underlined, annotated, and indexed before the exam session, but candidates may not write, highlight, underline, or index in the references during the examination session. The PSI bulletin also allows a silent, nonprinting, non-programmable calculator in the examination center. Because open book exams still require speed and accuracy, preparation should include regular practice using the code book and tabs. Knowing where to find answers is just as important as understanding the electrical concepts behind the questions. The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs is especially useful for building reference navigation skills. During study, candidates can practice locating chapters, articles, tables, definitions, exceptions, and calculation rules.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: Repetition helps reduce wasted time and improves confidence when answering code questions under timed exam conditions.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t:
Alaska electrical administrator applicants must obtain approval from the State of Alaska before sitting for the examination. The process begins by submitting the appropriate Electrical Administrator application and required supporting documentation to the State of Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing. Online applications are filed through a MyAlaska account, and paper applications are also available through the state licensing page.
After the State of Alaska reviews and approves the application, the applicant may schedule the examination through PSI. Once the exam is passed, examination results must be submitted to the Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing. Alaska states that examination results are valid for one year.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Alaska electrical administrators are regulated by the State of Alaska Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development, Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing. The division staffs the electrical administrator program, carries out licensing regulation, makes final licensing decisions, and handles disciplinary action for violations of licensing laws. Electricians in Alaska are separately regulated by the Department of Labor, Labor Standards and Safety, Mechanical Inspection Section. This distinction is important for candidates because Alaska electrical work and contractor supervision may involve different regulatory responsibilities depending on the credential, work category, and business structure. The Unlimited Commercial Wiring Administrator category covers supervision of inside wiring work under Alaska law.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Inside wiring includes electrical work subject to the National Electrical Code within buildings and within property lines, beginning at the secondary side of the transformer or applicable point of attachment for conductors serving buildings or structures within the property lines. The category does not include linework consisting of poles and towers, including wires, cables, and apparatus supported by them, or outdoor substations or work defined under the unlimited linework category. Candidates preparing for Alaska master electrician or electrical administrator work should study both trade knowledge and Alaska-specific statutes and regulations. The exam content outline includes Alaska statutes and regulations as a tested area, so preparation should not be limited to NEC study alone.

pieces.t: PSI lists the Unlimited Commercial Wiring Administrator exam as 100 questions with a required passing score of 70% and a time allowance of 240 minutes.

pieces.h: Q: What topics should I study for the Alaska master electrician exam pathway?
pieces.t: Important study areas include general electrical knowledge, grounding and bonding, services, feeders, branch circuits, raceways and enclosures, conductors and cables, special occupancies, motors, lighting, low-voltage systems, photovoltaics, alarm systems, safety, and Alaska statutes and regulations.

pieces.h: Q: How should I use the NEC tabs while studying?
pieces.t: Use the tabs to organize major NEC sections and practice locating information quickly. The best approach is to combine tabbed navigation with repeated practice so you understand both where information is located and how to apply it to exam-style questions.
